statusDetail: Coverage-complete external audit. A persistent loading overlay blocked visual interaction, but rendered DOM and independent evidence primitives permitted all atomic checks to be judged.

principleOutcomes.reason: Target.com is an intentionally US English retail surface in this audit and no alternate locale or writing-mode route was exposed. The audited public surface is single-locale en-US and did not expose user-entered locale-sensitive dates or currency conversion. No scheduling, recurring event, or user-authored time-zone flow was exposed in the audited paths.

No declared agent-facing intent was provided; WebMCP is emerging and absence is treated as an opportunity, not a failure. No page task required summarization or language-model inference, and no declared on-device AI intent was provided.

paths.description: Homepage and global shell: first impression, navigation, preferences, responsive layout, performance, security, and discoverability.
Category/listing archetype represented by the backpacks category; checked listing chrome and persistent runtime overlay.
Search-results archetype and start of the primary product-discovery journey.
Product-detail archetype: title, price, fulfillment and add-to-cart actions.
Cart/checkout entry archetype and end of the anonymous primary flow.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is visually identical to the light capture, and the computed root color-scheme is normal with a white body background.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: An indefinite loading animation remains active under reduced motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched reduce but still found a 550 ms animation with an indefinite iteration count on the persistent loader.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable the non-essential spinner animation under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and use a static status affordance.

findings.summary: A modal loading screen obscures every audited commerce surface indefinitely.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, search, product, category, and cart screenshots show a modal “Almost there…” overlay; after 15 seconds it remained display:flex and visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the blocking overlay as soon as critical content is ready, impose a timeout, and expose retry/dismiss recovery when initialization fails.

findings.summary: The blocking overlay is an ad-hoc role=dialog with no user dismissal.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence identifies a DIV role=dialog/aria-modal=true; the persistent overlay has no visible close, cancel, or retry action.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog only for a genuinely modal operation, provide cancel/retry, and close it deterministically; avoid modal UI for passive loading.

findings.summary: The representative search-to-product-to-cart journey is visually blocked.
findings.evidence: Search results and product details were present in the DOM, but all journey screenshots remained covered by the loader, preventing pointer completion of selection and add-to-cart.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat initialization failures as recoverable and never leave the purchase path behind a permanent modal loading state.

findings.summary: The loading state provides no recovery action or useful progress.
findings.evidence: After 15 seconds the only message remained “Almost there… Thank you for your patience,” with no timeout, retry, cancel, or fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a bounded loading timeout with clear failure copy and retry/back controls while preserving page context.

findings.summary: Lab load performance misses the good Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.7 s and TBT about 2,000 ms, with a performance score of 0.35; the independent trace was faster but still recorded blocking work.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritize the hero resource, and defer non-critical scripts and media.

findings.summary: Heavy JavaScript blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported about 2,000 ms TBT; the trace recorded five long tasks, a 248.73 ms maximum task, and 303.95 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, delay analytics/ads, and schedule non-critical work by priority.

findings.summary: The homepage delivers a large, fragmented critical path.
findings.evidence: HAR evidence recorded 208 requests and 5.75 MB transferred, including 19 stylesheets and at least ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheet candidates; 2.91 MB was one media resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/media, and prioritize only LCP-critical assets.

findings.summary: Substantial unused JavaScript is shipped on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 634 KiB of unused JavaScript; HAR recorded 87 scripts and 2.08 MB of script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and interaction, remove duplicate/unused bundles, and conditionally load third parties.

findings.summary: Some visible labels do not match their accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s label-content-name-mismatch audit failed, despite an otherwise strong 0.99 accessibility score.
findings.suggestedFix: Align each control’s accessible name with its visible label and re-run axe/Lighthouse.

findings.summary: The heading hierarchy is not sequential.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the DOM starts with an H2 sign-in prompt before H1, then jumps from H1 to H3 cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the page H1 the first structural heading and use sequential heading levels for sections and cards.

findings.summary: Chrome reports unresolved inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the inspector-issues audit and recorded third-party-cookie concerns; the HAR also contained eight 403 responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools Issues, failed resources, and third-party compatibility warnings before release.

findings.summary: Multiple cookies are not marked Secure and an auth-like token is script-readable.
findings.evidence: The cookie primitive counted 24 insecure/problematic cookies, including ffsession, TealeafAkaSid, AMCV cookies and sddStore without Secure; idToken lacked HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all state cookies Secure, use appropriate SameSite, and keep authentication tokens HttpOnly unless a documented architecture requires otherwise.

findings.summary: The homepage has a broad tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Trackers found 33 third-party origins and five known tracker hosts; HAR attributed 187/208 requests and 5.67 MB to non-www.target.com origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit third-party necessity, gate non-essential tracking on consent, batch analytics, and remove vendors without measurable user value.

findings.summary: Browser policy headers are incomplete and referrer policy is permissive.
findings.evidence: Headers showed no Permissions-Policy; Referrer-Policy was no-referrer-when-downgrade. CSP only declared frame-ancestors, leaving script/style policy unenforced in this header.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a complete CSP, a restrictive Permissions-Policy, and strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy.

findings.summary: Runtime initialization does not converge to a usable state.
findings.evidence: The same loading dialog stayed visible after 15 seconds across independent loads, while underlying content had rendered.
findings.suggestedFix: Make initialization idempotent, detect failed dependencies, and always settle the loading state into content or actionable error UI.

findings.summary: No web app manifest or offline fallback was evident for this app-like commerce experience.
findings.evidence: Recon found no manifest link. A service-worker-capable runtime exists, but no install metadata or tested offline fallback was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid manifest and a minimal offline/retry shell for browsed products and cart context, or explicitly scope out installability.

findings.summary: Failed dependencies lead to an indefinite loader rather than recovery.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded eight HTTP 403 responses and all tested paths remained under the loading modal with no retry or fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle dependency failures explicitly and transition from loading to a retryable partial-content state.

findings.summary: Input autocomplete semantics are too generic.
findings.evidence: The recon probe found the email-address field using autocomplete="on" rather than the specific email token; the search input deliberately uses off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="email" and other purpose-specific tokens on customer data fields.

findings.summary: Commercial actions cannot be completed reliably in the observed state.
findings.evidence: Product price and Add to cart were present in DOM evidence, but product and cart screenshots remained blocked by the indefinite modal.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a clear, reversible product-to-cart path and show an actionable failure state if dependencies fail.

findings.summary: Images are not consistently responsive or dimensioned.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found five oversized images, 18 without srcset, and all 38 missing at least one explicit dimension; the page does use WebP query delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide width and height, responsive srcset/sizes, and request dimensions close to rendered size.

findings.summary: Large background and third-party work is disproportionate to the initial retail task.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 208 requests, 87 scripts, 187 cross-origin requests, and a 2.91 MB media transfer while an indefinite loader continued animating.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer ads, analytics, and decorative media until needed; stop work when obscured/backgrounded and impose a page-weight budget.

findings.summary: Third-party and media transfer dominates the homepage.
findings.evidence: 5.67 MB of 5.75 MB was from origins other than www.target.com; one media asset was 2.91 MB and known ad/session-replay trackers loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Set vendor and media budgets, defer non-essential media, and remove or lazy-load tracking code.

findings.summary: The search results page has a large baseline heap footprint.
findings.evidence: The search baseline heap contained 1,455,397 nodes, 6,810,817 edges, and 69.7 MB self size, including 117,103 closures.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained objects and closures, virtualize result content where useful, and unload inactive vendor modules.
